findings_to_judge.finding: Building Q2 FY27 revenue bottom-up from Wealthfront's own published monthly assets (May: cash $45.0bn / advisory $54.0bn; June: cash $44.8bn / advisory $54.3bn) at the company's own last-reported annualised take rates (cash 0.58%, advisory 0.21%) gives ~$94.5m even assuming July was flat with June, versus a sell-side consensus near $98.0m and an FY27 consensus of $384.9m that requires ~$98m in each remaining quarter.

The mechanical driver of the cash take-rate compression — the 'Direct Deposit Plus' 25bp permanent APY uplift — launched 2026-03-02, so it was live for two of the three months of Q1 FY27 (when the cash rate fell 0.61%->0.58%) and for all three months of Q2 FY27, against a disclosed asset-weighted cross-product adoption of over 63% at June-end and rising.

findings_to_judge.finding: Wealthfront's annualized cash management fee rate is running below its own guide and still falling — the company guided ~0.59% for fiscal Q1 2027, printed 0.58%, and the CFO disclosed on the 2026-06-04 call that the May-end rate was 54 basis points; the cause is the 'Direct Deposit + Investing' +0.25% APY boost launched 2026-03-02 which carries no expiration and no balance cap, so it compounds mechanically as asset-weighted cross-product adoption rises (61% at FY26 year-end, 62.5% at April, over 63% at June).

Fiscal Q2 2027 is a structurally mismatched quarter: it covers 2026-05-01 to 2026-07-31, during which the Fed did not move (held 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29, unchanged since December 2025) so no rate benefit accrued, while Wealthfront Home Lending only launched in California and Texas on 2026-08-11 — after quarter end — meaning the full pre-launch mortgage build cost sits in Q2 with essentially zero mortgage revenue, on top of Q1 GAAP expenses already up 46% year-over-year to $75.9m against 7% revenue growth.

Schwab disclosed on 2026-08-14 that transactional sweep cash fell $8.9bn in July 2026 to $476.8bn — 1.8% of the balance in one month — 'reflecting client net purchasing activity as well as typical seasonality related to advisory fee payments', and the S&P 500 then rose 2.7% in August to record highs; at Wealthfront a dollar migrating from cash to investing loses roughly 60% of its revenue (cash fee rate ~54bp vs investment advisory running ~21bp annualised on $26.2m of quarterly revenue against ~$50bn of advisory assets), so the same client behaviour that will produce a record platform-assets headline tonight is revenue-dilutive.

The rate regime that defines this company's entire bear case has flipped: the FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29 with three regional presidents dissenting in favour of a 25bp HIKE, and futures price roughly 60% odds of a hike at the 2026-09-16 meeting one week after this print — while Wealthfront has held its base Cash Account APY at 3.30% since 2026-01-30 and its own 10-K states that 'in weaker macroeconomic environments with higher interest rates, our cash management products become more popular.'

Tonight is a double-disclosure event, not a normal print: because Wealthfront publishes monthly metrics only for the first two months of each fiscal quarter, the 2026-08-19 scheduling release states that metrics 'through August 2026' will be posted with the results — meaning July (fiscal Q2's third month) and August (fiscal Q3's first month) flows both become public for the first time tonight, alongside the P&L.
